A very small amount of material — on the order of 100 grams to less than 2 kilograms, typically calcium carbonate (a common mineral found in limestone and used in products such as toothpaste) — would be released into a small mixed volume roughly 1 km long and 100 meters in diameter. The gondola would then fly back through that plume to measure aerosol microphysics, chemistry, and light scattering. A 2021 platform test in Sweden, planned with the Swedish Space Corporation from Esrange, was a hardware test only: the SCoPEx Advisory Committee recommended suspending it pending societal engagement, and no particles were to be released. In March 2024 Harvard announced that Keutsch was no longer pursuing SCoPEx; the platform is expected to be repurposed for stratospheric research unrelated to solar geoengineering.

They found that chemtrails language dominates that discourse, that conspiracy narratives spill over across countries, and that Twitter volume surged around reporting on Harvard's SCoPEx project — including a peak near the April 2017 launch, on the order of 8,000 tweets. A consortium of funders supporting related solar geoengineering research included the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation; Bill Gates is a frequent target of conspiracy narratives. Funding climate or geoengineering research is not evidence of a covert aircraft spraying program. In the 2018–2021 window, Debnath et al. report that chemtrails talk became semantically broader, more toxic, and more tied to demands to stop alleged spraying, while a smaller stream of tweets discussed legitimate environmental concerns such as ozone, biodiversity, and mitigation.

Meeting Paris temperature goals requires deep, sustained cuts in fossil CO2, methane and other greenhouse gases, plus protection of carbon sinks — not covert aviation spraying.
